featured_reviews.name: Falguni P
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kids Friendly place.
This place is divided into different sections, the entry is free.

*Fish park - this park is quite big and has 3 gates,
The first half has fish tanks, selfie point and a fountain
Currently there are only few fishes, the fountain is shut and the empty tanks are not maintained well (due to COVID)

*The cricket ground - usually there is local cricket match on weekends, chairs are provided for audience.

*Kids play area- there are slides, swings, and play area for kids.

*Open Gym- they have a gym area near the second gate, which is currently closed for public, equipments are mainted nicely.

*Walking / jogging track - there is a long walking and jogging track around the park, local residents usually come visit for morning and evening walks

*Accessibility - park is partially Accessibility as there are stairs in some parts of the park. This place is ideal for kids, family and senior citizens.
The fish park gate is accessible but to reach the other area it is ideal to use the second gate which has a slope.

featured_reviews.name: Cletus Dias
featured_reviews.review_text: The Fish Park was one of my favorite park for walks. Over the years and especially after the pandemic, it has lost its charm. featured_reviews.review_text: There are about 10 acquariums. But they need cleaning. The park needs to be maintained. There are fibre decorations in the park those were full of dust. featured_reviews.name: J T
featured_reviews.review_text:
Khar Gymkhana, an iconic club has become a hub for a wide range of indoor and outdoor sports. The club offers excellent facilities for games like table tennis, billiards, cards, tennis, cricket etc.
The Pavilion restaurant is well-known for its excellent menu of  food and drinks.

Membership to Khar Gymkhana is exclusive, with life membership available to individuals either within the immediate family or those married into a family that holds membership.

We enjoyed a nice dinner. The food was delicious, and the service was fast. From the starters to the desserts, everything—whether vegetarian or non-vegetarian—was prepared well. Ambience is wonderful. Overall we had a goid time with family.

featured_reviews.name: Zerlina Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is exclusively for its members but if you know a member you can tag along with them as their guest. Their food is good and worth a try.. They also have a huge sports section where you can go for tennis cricket as well. Well memtained as well.

featured_reviews.name: Amit Mehra
featured_reviews.review_text: We were two for tea and snacks around 5.30pm. Got a table easily . Service was quick . We ordered sev puri - very crisp n right amount of spice . The masala dal on top added a nice crunch. The wet bhel was a bit sweet and we asked them to add some more spice which they did - so it turned out quite good . Final dish was the grilled veg sandwich which was also very good . The masala chai was hot and flavourful and the coffee was hot and good too .

featured_reviews.name: kartik sharma
featured_reviews.review_text: Had a great experience here, visited here for the 1st time. Loved the restaurant Pavilion. Affordable food and drinks with good quality. The ambiance over all is amazing. Will visit again soon.

featured_reviews.name: Bharat mulani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Yesterday  celebrated my Mom's birthday their.
As entry is only for members so we went through  one of the member known to my nephew.
Guests charges apply for every person.
But the quality of food was too good n ambience was also very pleasant.  Live singer was there. As it was a weekday so not very crowded.
If you are a member  than lucky you can enjoy all the facilities but  if not then if possible try to go with the known  source.  Worth going their.
Rates are very reasonable  n staff is very courteous.

featured_reviews.name: Vijayshri
featured_reviews.review_text:
Khar Gymkhana, an iconic club founded in the late 1920s by a group of influential sports enthusiasts, has a rich history of nurturing talent and hosting prestigious tournaments. Over the decades, it has become a hub for a wide range of indoor and outdoor sports. The club offers excellent facilities for games like table tennis, billiards, cards, tennis, cricket, and swimming. In addition to the sports, Khar Gymkhana also boasts a popular restaurant called The Pavilion, known for its diverse menu of  food and drinks.

Membership to Khar Gymkhana is exclusive, with life membership available to individuals either within the immediate family or those married into a family that holds membership. There are also other types of memberships that can be obtained.

During our visit, we enjoyed a nice lunch and had time to observe some of the ongoing activities and games around the club. The food was delicious, and the service was surprisingly fast, considering the large crowd the restaurant was catering to. From the starters to the desserts, everything—whether vegetarian or non-vegetarian—was prepared well. However, there was one issue: the club lacked sufficient wheelchairs. A senior citizen in our group had to wait for a while to get access to one, as it was already in use by another member.

featured_reviews.name: Buccaneer2.0
featured_reviews.review_text:

Khar Gymkhana, has been rooted long back due to the Cricket ground and lot of school official tournaments happen at this venue.

Though the facilities can be upgraded for all and not only for club members…like food facility for all, wheel chair access to the ground, etc.

Rest it gives you a very positive vibes.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Awesome experience. Yummy food with best company of your lovely friends.
Food was yummy.
To start with we  ordered Masala Papad.
Chicken Platter for Starters - chicken reshmi and malai kebab nice and juicy, chicken seekh kebab and chicken tikka was yum too. The special recommended starter of our friend's daughter the "Bombil Sandwich" was a hit.

review_photos.caption: Yummy Starter plate with Bombil Sandwich

featured_reviews.name: Lisette Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text: The OG Bandra Seafood place... Jai Hind Pali. Choose from a variety of thalis  - or if you're in a large group sample everything! From prawn curry and rice to chicken sukke with neer dosa and tisre, surmai, crab, bangda, bombil... you'll find it hard to go wrong at Jai Hind. Even the accompaniments hut the spot - rice papads, solkadi, techha, jawla...  Friendly and efficient wait staff. A bit small / cramped but worth going and getting your fish straight out of the pan - by the time it's delivered home it doesn't taste quite the same!

featured_reviews.name: Nicola
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is my absolute go-to place for Konkan style seafood. Every time I have been, it's delicious, and I have been lots. Good value for money and the food is always perfectly cooked. My favourites are Bombil sandwich ( heavenly), bombil fry, ambotik curry, green masala curry (Herrvi?), sukka tisrya, and the list goes on. I  usually combine with palak Khichdi, which is also devine. Neer dosa , chapati, and finish with a classic  caramel custard dessert.
Tiny little restaurant,  but seriously,  some of the best seafood in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Vedant Raut (Vedanta)
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Hind Lunch Home,  Pali Naka,  Bandra (west)

Jai Hind is a brightest shining star of the galaxy of coastal cuisine restaurants in Mumbai.  With the few branches spread across the city,  this branch at Bandra,  Pali Naka is their first branch.  The other one is on the Linking Road, which seems to be rather spacious and well furnished.  But as a foodie, my hunt is always for a 'Value for money'  restaurants with excellent quality and quantity and this desire of mime gets fulfilled only in humble homely restaurants.  This branch at Pali Naka has been renovated recently and has only five tables in all.  I recommend to reserve a table in the evening as its a very old and famous restaurant in the area and gets filled quite soon.

The list of dishes we ordered :

1.  Patra Ni Macchi (Basa)
2. Bombil Thali
3. Chicken Sukka Thali

Let me begin with the most yummiest first. The chicken sukka was simply top quality stuff made with supreme perfection. It was creamy with great blend of masalas and literally made us lick our fingers till the end.  The chicken pieces were one of the softest and well marinated ones I ever had.  The Bombil was crispy and crunchy on the outside and soft juicy within. The soul kadi (pink broth)  was thick and made with actual coconut milk.  The texture of the chapatis were homely and rice was soft, fresh and well cooked.

Patra Ni Macchi was steamed to ultimate perfection,  which retained the original flavour of the soft melting Basa fish.  The green stuffing on it was blend of spicy and sour.

Over all,  A must visit restaurant..
Staff is helpful

Update !!

Visited here last night.

What we had :

- Chicken Sukka thali - 5 stars 🤩- Delicious gravy with softest chicken.

- Egg Biryani  - 5 stars🤩  - Long grained rice with perfect blend of spices and 2 boiled eggs.

Check pics below 👇

Note : There are no washrooms here,  so I went to Janta Bar opposite to it,  to make me release.

featured_reviews.name: Ranajit Das
featured_reviews.review_text: I had a wonderful experience dining at Jai Hind Lunch Home in Pali Naka. The food was absolutely delicious, and the service was top-notch. The staff were extremely friendly and attentive, making sure that my dining experience was enjoyable from start to finish. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for authentic Indian cuisine in a welcoming atmosphere. Plus, the prices are very reasonable! Overall, a fantastic dining experience that I would definitely repeat.

featured_reviews.name: BHUPEN OZA
featured_reviews.review_text:
Once a Jesuit monastery, the magnificent mansion at Parel was built on the ruins of the old Vaijanath Temple. A traveller, Carsten Neibur had suggested the villa at Parel be called Sans Pareil (The Peerless) since nothing could compare with it in all of India.

Mr. W. Hornby (1771-1784) was the first Governor to take up residence at Parel. Melody and mellifluous voices filled the Durbar Hall. During these gala evenings, china and crystal would glitter under the chandeliers in the banquet hall. In 1804, diners raised their glasses at a banquet hosted by Gov. Jonathan Duncan to toast the launch of The Literary Society of Bombay.

Meanwhile, in Parel, industrialisation was asserting its noxious effect. The population had burgeoned. Pollutants fouled the air, creating conditions favoured by wind and water-borne diseases.

Governor Richard Temple transferred his residence to Malabar Point. In 1883 Lady Fergusson, wife of the Governor died of cholera in the Parel House. Following her death, Government House officially shifted to Malabar Point.

The Parel Residence was converted into a plague hospital where thousands received treatment for the plague that struck Bombay in 1897-98.

Dr Waldemar Haffkine entered the portals and developed the Plague and Cholera vaccines. Since 1925, this Government House is now known as The Haffkine Institute, in memory of the man who transformed a fortress into a citadel of science.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Abhay Chowdhary
featured_reviews.review_text: Haffkine Institute,Mumbai is a premier biomedical research institute of India established in 1899 as a Plague  Research Institute for control of Plague Epidemic under Dr Waldemar Mordecai Haffkine, an Ukrainian scientist who developed vaccines against Cholera and Bubonic Plague. The Plague Research Laboratory was renamed as," Bombay Bacteriology Laboratory" in 1906 and finally as, "Haffkine Institute" in 1925. The main Building of the Haffkine Institute is monumental premise  that has great historic significance. The building under Portuguese was acquired from Jesuit fathers in 1719. It was the first," RajBhavan" means Governor's Residence used by British Governor of Bombay Presidency. King Edward VII who visited India as Prince of Wales in 1895 had stayed here for a week.
